Weigh the cost of each strategy against the level of risk

All projects have risk. Strategies to manage risk come at a cost. For example, adding formal user reviews to manage the risk of user acceptance adds time and cost to the project. Carefully weigh the consequences of each project risk against the cost of strategies used to manage it.

Examine interdependencies of risks

When developing a strategy to manage risk, examine the relationships and dependencies among risks. A strategy to reduce risk in one area can increase risk in another. For example, a decision to reduce the risk of a lengthy project by increasing team size will increase the risk of ineffective team coordination and communication.
To act upon high risk rated future events that may impact the program before they become issues.

Element.attribute:
For each project risk, identify contingent actions that could be taken if a risk occurred.

Contingent actions are reactive and are invoked only if a risk actually occurs. For example,
if one of the project risks is that the hardware may not be installed in time for the planned
pilot site, identify contingent actions, such as an alternative pilot site. The process of
identifying contingent actions can require modifications to the project workplan to allow
more flexibility for these types of situations.

Document the contingent actions and adjust the plans as necessary.
